text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

Casas Bahia, Brazil's leading retailer in electronic goods and furniture, has suspended its purchases since the beginning of the month and plans to satisfy customer demand until the end of the year with existing stock.
The Central Bank has fined 11 brokerages and seven banks a total of $800 million for fraudulent exchange transactions in fictitious export operations.
-- CABRAL WINS DEBATE BUT WON'T CHANGE ELECTION TREND
Rio mayoral candidate Sergio Cabral is seen as having won a television debate with his adversary Luiz Paulo Conde, but this is unlikely to alter the election trend, which favors Conde.
-- SHOOTOUT CAUSES PANIC AND DEATH IN RIO CENTER
Robbers who assaulted a money exchange office in the center of Rio de Janeiro engaged in a gun battle with police in which one robber and one police officer were killed.
State oil giant Petrobras has broken the Brazilian oil production record with 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) in October, up from 880,000 bpd in September.
-- COST FOR MASS DISMISSAL MAY BE REDUCED
Mass dismissals of workers for economic reasons may become less costly under a proposal by the government, which aims to alter the way in which compensation for dismissed workers is calculated.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
